text:
Brothers,[^1] if someone is caught in any trespass, you who are spiritual should restore him in a spirit of gentleness. But watch yourself, or you too may be tempted.

[^1]: The Greek word refers to fellow believers, both men and women.

versions.text: Brothers, if someone is caught in a sin, you who are spiritual should restore him in a spirit of gentleness. But watch yourself, or you too may be tempted.
versions.explanation: The Greek ἔν τινι παραπτώματι includes the indefinite 'any,' which strengthens the sense; 'trespass' also reflects παράπτωμα (a false step, lapse) more precisely than the general 'sin.' A footnote on 'Brothers' clarifies the inclusive sense of ἀδελφοί for hearers.

text: Carry one another's burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
For if anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.
Let each one test his own work, and then he will have reason to boast in himself alone, and not in comparison with someone else.
For each will carry his own load.
The one who is taught the word should share all good things with the one who teaches.
Do not be deceived: God is not mocked. Whatever a person sows, that is what he will reap.
The one who sows to his own flesh will reap corruption from the flesh, but the one who sows to the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
So let us not grow weary of doing good, for at the right time we will reap a harvest, if we do not give up.
So then, as we have opportunity, let us do good to everyone, and especially to those who belong to the household of faith.
See what large letters I use as I write to you with my own hand.
Those who want to make a good showing in the flesh are the ones trying to compel you to be circumcised—only so that they will not be persecuted for the cross of Christ.
For not even those who are circumcised keep the law themselves; they want you circumcised so that they can boast about your flesh.
But may I never boast in anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
For neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything; what matters is a new creation.
Peace and mercy to all who walk by this rule, and to the Israel of God.

From now on, let no one cause me trouble, for I bear on my body the marks of Jesus.[^1]

[^1]: The Greek word refers to a brand or scar such as those marking a slave or servant; Paul means the scars from his sufferings for Christ.

versions.text: From now on, let no one trouble me, for I bear on my body the marks of Jesus.
versions.explanation: A brief footnote helps hearers understand στίγματα, which is otherwise obscure in English; 'cause me trouble' also reads a bit more naturally aloud than 'trouble me.'

text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.
